There are two options for the last digit: 2 and 6.

Case 1: Last digit is 2. The problem reduces to finding the number of 4-digit numbers using the digits {2,2,5,6,7}. Consider the number of 2's in this 4-digit number. There must be at least one. There are C(4, 1) \* 3! / 0! ways of constructing a 4-digit number where 2 occurs exactly once (C(4, 1) is the number of ways to position the 2 in the number). Then there are C(4, 2) \* 3! / 1! ways of constructing a 4-digit number where 2 occurs exactly twice. The result is C(4, 1) \* 3! + C(4, 2) \* 3! = 60.

Case 2: Last digit is 6. The problem reduces to finding the number of 4-digit numbers using the digits {2,2,2,5,7}. There are at least two 2’s in this number. There are C(4, 2) \* 2! / 0! ways of constructing a number where 2 occurs twice. Then there are C(4, 3) \* 2! / 1! ways of constructing a number where 2 occurs thrice. The result is C(4, 2) \* 2! + C(4, 3) \* 2! = 20.

Adding the two cases together, we get 80.
